claims.text: A uniform nanoscale copper coating can be deposited on tungsten surfaces by ALD before spark plasma sintering.
ALD copper pre-coating will lower the void fraction relative to conventional spark plasma sintering with untreated tungsten.
ALD copper pre-coating will reduce phase separation during sintering.
ALD-treated W-Cu composites will have higher thermal conductivity than composites produced by the stated untreated-tungsten SPS baseline.
ALD-treated W-Cu composites will have superior mechanical resilience under irradiation relative to the stated SPS baseline.
The starting composite consists of tungsten particles or connected tungsten regions embedded in a bulk copper matrix fabricated by spark plasma sintering.
ALD is typically conducted below 350 °C.
The proposed sintering is conducted well below tungsten's melting point and under conditions compatible with copper stability.
The deposition and sintering atmospheres are controlled to prevent oxidation.
The intended service boundary includes high heat flux and irradiation representative of fusion-reactor joints.
ALD copper pre-coating produces an atomically smooth, conformal copper interlayer at the tungsten-copper interface.
The conformal copper interlayer promotes interdiffusion at the tungsten-copper interface.
The conformal copper interlayer improves metallurgical bonding between tungsten and copper.
The ALD copper layer enhances the wettability of tungsten.
Enhanced interfacial wettability reduces void nucleation during sintering.
The ALD copper layer reduces phase separation during sintering.
The ALD copper layer fosters near-perfect contact between tungsten and copper.
Improved tungsten-copper interfacial contact reduces interfacial thermal barriers.
The improved interface increases durability against irradiation-induced stresses.
The long-term stability and performance of the ALD-induced interfacial layer under repeated thermal cycling and sustained irradiation are untested.
